title: Evaluating Intra-firm LLM Alignment Strategies in Business Contexts

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual analysis of user over-reliance on automated AI outputs and its subsequent impact on reducing human critical thinking, scrutiny, and moral deliberation within collaborative business workflows.

Theoretical examination of how pre-training data distributions and fine-tuning objectives implicitly embed specific political, ideological, and cultural viewpoints (e.g., Western vs. non-Western concepts) into an AI Assistant's perspective.

Normative ethical analysis using hypothetical intra-firm scenarios to illustrate how alignment strategies can either amplify or constructively challenge department-specific priorities (e.g., engineering speed vs. ethical rigor).
Ethical trade-off assessment detailing how 'supportive' AI alignment strategies can flatter users and reinforce ethically flawed managerial goals rather than objectively questioning them.
